---
title: "Before the workshop"
---

Four things are needed before the workshop, and each ends in something that you can check: R and the workspaces installed, with their setup checks reporting no failure; the first module on R worked through; the background page read; and the Eurobarometer files of the waves that the paper used downloaded to your machine, for the file of respondents that you build after the second day. The first day teaches the IDE and Quarto live, with the modules on the AR4DS website as its reading, so working through them beforehand gives you a head start but is not needed.

## 1. R and the workspace

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the [workspace of the Europeanisation and the economy case study](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace), and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure. The workshop's tasks are done in this workspace, with the slides of the second day and the browser lab as the fallback if an installation fails. The first day teaches R, the IDE and Quarto live on the file of the Housing and racial bias case study, the running example of the modules on the AR4DS website, so download the [workspace of the Housing case study](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace) as well and run its setup check too. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation will not cooperate, tell the facilitator before the workshop: the first day leaves time to finish it.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The module teaches the R that the workshop asks of you, from a first line of code to a table and a figure. It works on the data of the Housing case study, a file small enough to look at whole, and its blocks of code run in your browser.

## 3. Background {#the-case-study}

[Read the background](../../background.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The background page presents the original study and its data, the SCORE programme and the SCORE robustness study (Aczel et al. 2026), the five reanalyses and the replications. Every day of the workshop works on this case study.

## 4. The Eurobarometer files

[Download the Eurobarometer files](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-eurobarometer-files-for-the-individual-level-work){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The file of respondents that you build after the second day, on which the work on respondents of the third day rests, needs the Eurobarometer files of the waves that the paper used. The files come from the GESIS archive under a free account and on terms that do not allow the files to be passed on, so each participant downloads them to their own machine, and they never leave it. [The GESIS archive](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the module on data sources takes the download screen by screen. The workspace switches the AI features of Positron and VS Code off for its whole folder, for the reason set out in the [section on licensed data](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ai.html#sec-licensed) of the module on AI assistants.

**By the start of the workshop** you have the setup checks of both workspaces reporting no failure, you have worked through the first module on R, you know what the claim is and how far apart the results of the five analysts are, and the Eurobarometer files are on your machine.
